name: Antero Resources
description: Antero is a pure Appalachian Basin natural gas producer: it drills horizontal wells in the Marcellus Shale (mainly West Virginia) and sells gas, natural gas liquids (ethane, propane, butane) and a little oil. Unusually, 38 percent of 2025 revenue was NGLs, because much of its gas is liquids-rich, and it has bought large amounts of long-term pipeline capacity so it can ship gas to the Gulf Coast, Chicago and LNG export rather than sell at low local prices; the gathering, processing and transport bill ($2.27 per Mcfe) is the biggest cost. It owns 29 percent of Antero Midstream, which gathers its gas and supplies water. In February 2026 it bought HG Energy's West Virginia assets for $2.8 billion in cash and sold its Ohio Utica assets for $800 million.

hq.note: FY2025 10-K Items 1 and 2: "Our corporate headquarters is in Denver, Colorado"

employees.note: Full-time employees, of which 243 in production and operations and 184 in midstream and water (FY2025 10-K). Executives and some staff also serve Antero Midstream.

businessLines.name: Exploration and production
businessLines.how: It sells gas and NGLs at market prices (partly hedged) under firm sales and transport contracts to utilities, LNG exporters, Gulf Coast and Midwest buyers; revenue moves with Henry Hub gas and NGL prices times volume, and the largest costs are the fixed-fee gathering, processing and pipeline charges it pays.
businessLines.description: Drilling and producing natural gas, NGLs and oil in the Appalachian Basin; 3,442 MMcfe/d (1,256 Bcfe) in 2025; 19,149 Bcfe of proved reserves at 2025-12-31 (PV-10 $9,679M); 1,775 net productive wells.

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $66.3M, depressed by a low gas price year ($2.29 per Mcf)

businessLines.name: Marketing
businessLines.how: It does not make a profit: it resells unused firm pipeline capacity and purchased gas to offset the minimum-commitment fees Antero owes on capacity it does not fully use (10-K: net marketing costs of $0.02 to $0.04 per Mcfe expected in 2026); the segment loss is what the resales do not recover.
businessLines.description: Sells excess firm transportation capacity and buys and resells third-party gas and NGLs to offset pipeline minimum-commitment fees.

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 loss $(65.8)M; the 10-K guides to net marketing costs of $0.02 to $0.04 per Mcfe in 2026

businessLines.name: Equity method investment in Antero Midstream
businessLines.how: Fee-based gathering, compression and water services paid by Antero's E&P segment under long-term dedications covering substantially all of Antero's West Virginia and Ohio acreage; Antero shares in it through its 29% ownership.
businessLines.description: 29% of Antero Midstream Corporation's common stock at 2025-12-31; Antero Midstream provides gathering, compression, water handling and blending to Antero under long-term contracts (731 miles of gathering pipeline, 4.8 Bcf/d compression).

revenue.note: Antero Midstream's own revenue, nearly all from Antero's E&P segment; eliminated in consolidation, so not part of the $5,275.8M consolidated revenue

businessLines.revenueNote: Antero Midstream's own revenue, nearly all from Antero's E&P segment; eliminated in consolidation, so not part of the $5,275.8M consolidated revenue

operatingProfit.note: Antero's own result from it is its equity earnings and distributions on the 29% stake

brands.name: Martica Holdings LLC (Sixth Street joint venture)
brands.segment: Consolidated royalty-interest vehicle; 38 Bcfe of proved reserves attributable to the non-controlling interests at 2025-12-31
brands.share: Sixth Street reached its return hurdle on 2026-05-01 and Antero dissolved Martica on 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 10-Q)

whatsNext.text: 2026 capital budget $1.1B to $1.3B (including up to $200M discretionary growth capital) to complete 70 to 80 net horizontal wells
